newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed lower in dull quiet trade as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) reduced their positions amid profit-taking by speculators, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 3.08 points lower at 633.93.
"The market has been lacking genuine investment and share prices are unable to maintain their high levels as speculators booked profits at every rise," said Bharat Bhushan of brokers Nu Era Equity.
Traders said major investors kept to the sidelines ahead of the bourse regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) meet to announce steps to bolster market sentiment.

SEBI said after the board meeting on Tuesday that its board of directors decided to permit rights issues by mutual funds, subject to conditions that the existing unit holders were given repurchase facility at net asset value (NAV) related price.
SEBI took no steps to shore up prices on stock markets. "SEBI cannot push up prices or bring the prices down," SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told reporters.
Reliance Industries ended 1.40 rupees lower at 181.60 on profit-taking by speculators, brokers said.
ACC dropped 7.90 rupees to 955.50 on heavy selling by FIIs.
State Bank of India closed 3.65 rupees lower at 205.70, in line with the general trend.
Larsen and Toubro drifted 2.30 rupees lower to 199.
TELCO bucked the trend and gained 2.95 rupees to 304.85 on domestic institutional buying.
